ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure of rhombus $ABCD$, if $\angle ABC=80^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle BDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since ABCD is a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADC = \angle ABC = 80^\circ$, and DB bisects $\angle ADC$ and $\angle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDA = \angle BDC = 40^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle BDA = \boxed{40^\circ}$

method.method_draft: Use the rhombus diagonal angle-bisector property. First read from the image that ABCD is drawn as a rhombus with B on the left, D on the right, A at the top, C at the bottom, and diagonal BD drawn; the requested angle BDA is the angle between DB and DA at vertex D. From the text, take that ABCD is a rhombus and angle ABC is 80 degrees. Since opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, angle ADC equals angle ABC, so angle ADC = 80 degrees. In a rhombus, each diagonal bisects the angles at the vertices it connects, so diagonal DB bisects angle ADC. Therefore angle BDA is half of 80 degrees, giving 40 degrees.

method.method_draft: Use triangle ABD as an isosceles triangle instead of invoking the diagonal-bisector theorem. From the image, focus on the upper triangle ABD formed by sides AB, AD and diagonal BD; the target angle BDA is a base angle of this triangle. From the text, ABCD is a rhombus and angle ABC = 80 degrees. A rhombus is a parallelogram, so adjacent angles are supplementary; hence angle BAD = 180 - 80 = 100 degrees. Also, in a rhombus all sides are equal, so AB = AD, making triangle ABD isosceles with vertex angle BAD = 100 degrees. The two base angles ABD and BDA are equal and sum to 80 degrees, so each is 40 degrees. Thus angle BDA = 40 degrees.
